summary: Firefly Aerospace is the only private company with a successful Moon landing under its belt (Blue Ghost, 2025) and active NASA contracts for Moon Base construction. Alpha Flight 8 upcoming + $75M NASA MoonFall subcontract + Elytra orbital transfer vehicle in development. Buy-the-dip after SpaceX IPO selloff — secondary offering overhang cleared. KeyBanc Overweight $50, Jefferies $52. Moon case: Firefly becomes the Boeing of new space at $100+. Position max 3–5% — ค่าขนม ถ้า launch fails = ลง 50%+.

risks: Launch failure — Alpha rocket explosion = -40–60% same day (SpaceX history: every public failure = major selloff)
NASA budget cuts — Moon Base program dependent on Congressional appropriations; political risk real
SpaceX competition — Falcon 9/9R dominates commercial launch; Firefly competes in small sat segment only
Cash burn — space companies require constant capital; dilution is structural
Secondary offering overhang — recent $48 offering created technical resistance

macroRisk.rateOutlook: NASA contracts are government-appropriated — rate-insensitive. Commercial satellite launch revenue is tied to corporate capex but is multi-year contracted.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Rocket manufacturing is commodity-input intensive (aluminum, titanium, rocket fuel). Inflation squeezes margins but contract pricing is fixed-price government.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Space sector benefits from defense spending increases post-Ukraine/geopolitical risk. Bipartisan support for Moon program strong.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk LOW — revenue is NASA contract + government-backed. Rate environment secondary to launch success and contract awards.

postWin.note: Rocket Lab (RKLB) +45% on Electron launch success + NASA contract win (2023). Planet Labs +60% on manifest announcement. Space stocks have outsized reactions to successful launches.

postLose.note: ABL Space dissolved after RS1 failure (2023). Virgin Orbit -80% post-launch failure leading to bankruptcy. Launch failure is existential for early-stage launch companies.

spotSizing.reason: Space launch is binary by nature — rocket either flies or it doesn't. 3% max. FLY has proven track record (Alpha Flight 7 success, Blue Ghost moon landing) which reduces risk vs pure early-stage.
